How much lead-in? 0, 1 or 2

You heard pome become ipome at lead=2. The slot being added is not the carrier's i token — that sits one further back. It is the space, which acoustically holds the tail of that i.

That is the same region that holds a word's own vowel onset when the word starts with a vowel. So the one adjustment helps vowel-initial words and hurts consonant-initial ones. pome is the only consonant-initial word here — most Kinyarwanda nouns take a vowel prefix.
What I think the answer is: make the lead depend on the first sound. 2 slots for vowel-initial words, 0 for consonant-initial. For every word below except pome that means today's clip is already right; for pome it means the lead=0 column. Going to 1 everywhere is the simpler alternative — judge whether it still rescues avoka.

Two questions. Does pome at lead=0 sound right? And does avoka still have its opening a at lead=1 — because if it does, a single global lead=1 is simpler than branching on the first letter.
